cleanIntro: The EOS-AK is the AK model of US Palm's EOS suppressor line: a 718 Inconel can on a 14x1mm direct thread, held on the rifle by a locking collar that engages the AKM's muzzle detent. US Palm's book prints no way of taking the can itself apart. Its cleaning, approximately every 1000 rounds, is done with the can off the rifle: look inside and out, shake it, brush the threads, and a light film of oil on the outside. The interior wash — suppressor solvent or an ultrasonic cleaner, a warm-water rinse and compressed air — is the deep clean. Everything about unloading your rifle comes from that rifle's own manual.

steps.title: Cool, unloaded, magazine out, safety on
steps.action: Let the suppressor cool after shooting. Then make sure the rifle is completely unloaded, with the magazine removed and the safety engaged, before a hand goes near the muzzle.
steps.prose: US Palm's book covers the suppressor, not the rifle: how your rifle is unloaded and checked comes from its own manual.
steps.quote: Wait for the suppressor to cool after use and ensure the firearm is completely unloaded with the magazine removed and the safety engaged.
steps.cite: US Palm EOS Suppressors Operation & Safety Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — REMOVAL, p.18

steps.title: ⛔ Hot can: gloves, and somewhere safe to rest it
steps.action: A suppressor stays hot long after firing. Wait for it to cool before you take it off; if it has to come off hot, wear protective gloves. Rest the rifle where the can touches nothing that heat can damage, with the muzzle still pointed somewhere safe.
steps.prose: A can that has just been shot looks exactly like a cold one.
steps.quote: Suppressor is hot after use, allow the suppressor to cool before removal and/or service.
steps.cite: US Palm EOS Suppressors Operation & Safety Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — FIREARMS SAFETY — Burn Risk, p.8
steps.warn: If suppressor must be removed or installed when hot, protective gloves should be worn.

steps.title: Off the rifle with a wrench, then by hand
steps.action: Fit a wrench of the right size and loosen the suppressor until it turns by hand, then unscrew it from the barrel, taking care not to damage the threads.
steps.prose: This is US Palm's removal page for its direct-thread cans. The EOS-AK's own page covers only putting the can on, so it does not say whether the locking collar's 3mm hex screw or the rifle's detent has to be released first. If the can will not turn without force, stop and call US Palm rather than putting more on it.
steps.aside: Remove the suppressor from the barrel, taking care not to damage the threads.
steps.quote: Using a wrench of appropriate size, loosen the suppressor until it can be removed from the barrel by hand.
steps.cite: US Palm EOS Suppressors Operation & Safety Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — REMOVAL, p.18

steps.title: ⛔ That is as far as it goes
steps.action: With the can off the rifle the strip is done. US Palm prints no procedure for taking the EOS-AK apart, and its book forbids modifying any component of the suppressor unless the manual says to.
steps.prose: Anything past this point is US Palm's: they want a return authorization before a can is sent back.
steps.quote: NEVER MODIFY ANY OF THE COMPONENTS OF YOUR SUPPRESSOR UNLESS SPECIFICALLY INSTRUCTED TO DO SO IN THIS MANUAL.
steps.cite: US Palm EOS Suppressors Operation & Safety Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — FIREARMS SAFETY, p.10

no.q: NEVER MODIFY ANY OF THE COMPONENTS OF YOUR SUPPRESSOR UNLESS SPECIFICALLY INSTRUCTED TO DO SO IN THIS MANUAL.
no.src: US Palm EOS Suppressors Operation & Safety Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — FIREARMS SAFETY, p.10

steps.title: Look inside for debris and cracks
steps.action: Look into the suppressor's interior for anything that should not be there and for cracks. Then look over the outside for cracks and dents, especially around the muzzle end.
steps.prose: US Palm's inspection comes first in its cleaning list, every time, approximately every 1000 rounds — sooner after rain, mud, sand or saltwater.
steps.aside: Visual inspection of the outer surfaces for cracks and dents, especially in the muzzle area.
steps.quote: Visual inspection of the interior for foreign particles and cracks.
steps.cite: US Palm EOS Suppressors Operation & Safety Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, p.22

steps.title: Shake it and listen
steps.action: Shake the suppressor and listen for loose particles inside.
steps.prose: Anything you can hear moving, a crack or a dent is a reason to call US Palm, not to fire it and see.
steps.quote: Shake the suppressor to determine if any loose particles are audible.
steps.cite: US Palm EOS Suppressors Operation & Safety Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, p.22

steps.title: Brush and degrease the threads
steps.action: With a small brush, clean and degrease the threads — the rifle's muzzle threads and the can's own — and look them over for damage.
steps.prose: Carbon on these threads is what stops the can going on square, and a square fit is what keeps a bullet clear of the baffles.
steps.quote: Clean and degrease the muzzle thread and/or the contact surfaces on the flash hider / compensator with a small brush and inspect for defects.
steps.cite: US Palm EOS Suppressors Operation & Safety Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, p.22

steps.title: A light film of oil on the outside
steps.action: Wipe the outside of the can and, if you like, leave a light film of oil on it. Use only products made for firearms, and no wire brush on the outside.
steps.prose: Oil goes on the outside only — nothing is run through the bore.
steps.quote: The exterior of the suppressor may be coated with a light film of oil.
steps.cite: US Palm EOS Suppressors Operation & Safety Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, p.22
steps.warn: USE OF WIRE BRUSHES ON EXTERIOR SURFACES CAN PERMANENTALLY SCRATCH OR MAR THE FINISH.

deepSteps.title: Wash the interior: suppressor solvent or ultrasonic
deepSteps.action: With the can off the rifle, clean the interior with a solvent made for suppressors, or in an ultrasonic cleaner. Whichever you use, the cleaning solution must be one recommended for suppressors.
deepSteps.prose: US Palm names Breakthrough Clean Technologies as an example. Nothing comes apart for this: the can is washed whole.
deepSteps.aside: Take care to use a cleaning solution recommended for suppressors.
deepSteps.quote: The interior may be cleaned using Suppressor specific solvent such as Breakthrough Clean Technologies® or with an ultrasonic cleaner.
deepSteps.cite: US Palm EOS Suppressors Operation & Safety Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, p.22
deepSteps.warn: DO NOT RUN CLEANING PATCHES THROUGH THE SUPPRESSOR BORE.

deepSteps.title: Rinse with warm water
deepSteps.action: Rinse the suppressor with warm water to carry the solvent and loosened fouling out.
deepSteps.prose: What comes out carries lead: keep it off your skin and wash your hands afterwards.
deepSteps.quote: Rinse the suppressor and, if applicable, the flash hider/compensator with warm water.
deepSteps.cite: US Palm EOS Suppressors Operation & Safety Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, p.22

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Blow it out and let it drain completely
deepSteps.action: Blow the suppressor out with compressed air, then leave it until it has drained completely. No water or solvent may be left inside when it goes back on the rifle.
deepSteps.prose: Wear eye protection and aim the air away from you.
deepSteps.quote: Blow out the suppressor and, if applicable, the flash hider/compensator with compressed air.
deepSteps.cite: US Palm EOS Suppressors Operation & Safety Manual — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, p.22
deepSteps.warn: Using a suppressor containing water or other fluids will destroy the suppressor and firearm and cause injury or death to the user and bystanders.

cleaning.name: INSPECT
tasks: Interval: approximately every 1000 rounds — more often after rain, mud, sand or saltwater
Interior looked at for foreign particles and cracks
Outside looked at for cracks and dents, especially at the muzzle end
Shaken and listened to for loose particles

cleaning.name: THREADS
tasks: Muzzle threads cleaned and degreased with a small brush

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Light film of oil on the outside, if wanted
Only cleaning and lubrication products made for firearms
Do not use a wire brush on the outside: it scratches the finish
⛔ Never run cleaning patches through the suppressor bore

reassembly: Inside drained completely, with no water or solvent left in it.
Rifle unloaded, magazine removed, safety engaged.
Tighten the locking collar onto the suppressor until it stops, then back it off one full turn.
Thread the suppressor onto the rifle.
When the rifle's detent begins to engage the locking collar, engage the detent and thread the collar on by itself, toward the rifle.
When the detent is at full engagement and another turn would miss the detent slot, hand tighten the suppressor firmly.
Tighten the 3mm hex screw on the locking collar.
Check bore alignment, per the book's Bore Alignment page, before firing.
fncheck: Rifle still unloaded, magazine out, safety on: the can is hand tight, the rifle's detent sits in the locking collar's slot and the collar's 3mm hex screw is tight. Check bore alignment before the first shot — US Palm says never fire a suppressor on a new host without verifying it: insert an alignment rod from the muzzle end; resistance means an alignment problem to fix before shooting. If you are unsure of the result, US Palm says to consult a professional gunsmith.
